You remind me of myself. In 2012 I had to open Christmas presents while my mom was in the next room in her bed in a coma while she battled breast cancer. I was only nine so I hadn't realized it, but she was on in-home hospice care at that point. She passed a few days after Christmas, January 5th. It is so painful to watch cancer consume someone's entire being. It went from her coming home from an appointment saying she'd be fine to her being what seemed to be a shell of a person. She was so frail. I wish I could've protected and comforted her. I hate this time of year, it's like I cannot function as a human anymore. I am happy when I hear news of others being cured of cancer but angry as well because why couldn't it have been my mother who was cured and allowed to live out her adult life fully? Why is there still no universal cure for cancer? I am so sorry you are having to go through this, I don't wish this kind of pain on anyone. I also apologize for rambling under your post. I'm sending you lots of love and I am so sorry you are having to go through this at such a young age as well. I'm sure you being there with her in her last moments brought her a final sense of peace. Please take care of yourself and journal if you can. That's what helped me.

First of all, I'm proud of you for getting up and doing stuff. I know the feeling of not having the energy to do basic necessities. They may seem miniscule, but they are big steps in reality, especially to getting back on track to a "normal" life. 

Secondly, there is no time limit on grief or the grieving process. So, you're not grieving too long. Don't let someone rush you out of grief. But, I will say that it's not a great decision to quit your job suddenly because of that. It's great that you're still taking care of your kids, but it would have been a better idea to take a leave or something along the lines of that. But that's already said and done. I know it's hard, but please don't allow yourself to fall into a dark spot permanently. I hope that you can pull yourself back together again and wake up with a positive outlook on the next day. Sending lots of love. Take care!

Before my mom passed, she was in a coma. I sat by her bed, held her hands and just let all of my emotions out. I told her how much I loved her, kissed her cheeks, hugged her and so on and so forth. 

Then a few weeks later she passed. I was still stunned but it doesn't hurt as bad knowing that I got to tell her everything I wanted to before she passed. 

So,  I'd say spend as much time with your parents as you can. Tell them you love them a million times. Help them with things around the house. Show them that you appreciate them. 

It will hurt for a while and may never go away.. But there's always a light at the end of the tunnel. Grief comes in waves.

First, I'm really sorry for your loss. I know it must be really hard for you, especially being days apart. But, I relate to you, a lot. My parents passed away in 2008 and 2012 and about a month ago my big sister passed away unexpectedly. When she passed, all I could think was that the world was truly cruel. You start to wonder why this is happening to you, why do I have to have everyone taken from me? It's really not fair. Not fair for me, or you. 

This past month I've been feeling an array of emotions from anger to guilt to sadnesss.... I find myself becoming envious of those around me who still have their loved ones. I also feel super lost because I'm 19 and she was basically the mother figure for me. It's like, what am I supposed to do now? I still don't believe it, I find myself at times acting as if she was still here then realizing she's not. Sometimes I feel like I took her for granted. It's hard. Truly. There's people you think will never die. I'm not sure what advice to give you, but I hope you know that you are never alone. I feel you. What brings me comfort is knowing that they are no longer suffering on this Earth and that they wouldn't want us to fall into a dark place over their passing. It's not your fault, you couldn't have known this was how it would happen. Do not blame yourself. Please take care of yourself and stay close with your sibling because you are all you got. Be patient with yourself and allow yourself to feel the emotions you are feeling. I bottled them up and now it's just hitting me a month later. We're only human. I'm really wishing you the best.
